doc.title: Anat Cohen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 9, 2021

title: DownBeat polls and the mystery of the clarinet's appeal
summary: She cannot explain her poll success, recalls playing one clarinet tune per show, and notes the Benny Goodman stereotype.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: You’ve done very well in the polls, DownBeat, in the last few years, and I wonder if people who are voting for you, if it’s more than the way — how am I — I’m trying to say that people will like what you do not just because of the way you play your instrument, it’s the music you choose to play, at least this is my attitude. Do you think part of your success in those pollings have to do with what you’ve done with combining music and the variety of things you present?

I don’t know. I don’t know, the mystery of the clarinet, and I talked about it at the beginning of our conversation, the certain natural connection. And at the time I remember my first shows as a band leader I played tenor saxophone for the whole show and I played one song on the clarinet, because at the beginning I was, as I mentioned, the clarinet took over my life, right? I was playing saxophone and clarinet was there waiting, lurking, in the corner. So I would play one song on the clarinet in the whole show and then people would come to talk to me after the show and they would just talk about the clarinet. And I was like okay, but also saying okay maybe the way I play it, I don’t know, it reaches them. I don’t know. I don’t have a reason. I don’t think I’m a better clarinetist than so many others, and everybody has something to offer. So this is all one big mystery for me. But I’m grateful for people to, first of all to accepting the clarinet as an instrument they are willing to listen to and to like, which is already a big step. So many people have preconceptions about the clarinet and they associate it — you know you say jazz and clarinet and people still say, “Ah, Benny Goodman.” And I’m like okay yes, Benny Goodman but there’s more to it than this. So that’s all I am trying to do.
